title: Multi-Modal Domain Adaptation Across Video Scenes for Temporal Video Grounding

problems.name: Domain Shift and Generalization
problems.evidence_sentence: Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: • We present the first attempt to explore the unsupervised domain adaptation setting across video scenes for the temporal video grounding task, which poses a challenging multi-modal cross-domain problem. • To enhance performance in new target scenes, we introduce a novel method called Adversarial-based Multimodal Domain Adaptation (AMDA).

problems.name: Spatio-Temporal and Object/Event-Level Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: Thus, to address this issue and enhance model performance on new scenes, we explore the TVG task in an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) setting across scenes for the first time, where the video-query pairs in the source scene (domain) are labeled with temporal boundaries, while those in the target scene are not.

problems.name: Boundary Ambiguity and Localization Precision
problems.evidence_sentence: Supervised methods require a large number of precise temporal boundary labels to train discriminative models, which is highly labor-intensive and time-consuming.

methods.name: Object/Event/Spatio-Temporal Modules

methods.name: Benchmark or Dataset Construction
methods.evidence_sentence: Under the UDA setting, we introduce a novel Adversarial Multi-modal Domain Adaptation (AMDA) method to adaptively adjust the model's scene-related knowledge by incorporating insights from the target data.

methods.name: Boundary Refinement and Temporal Clustering
methods.evidence_sentence: Multi-Modal Domain Adaptation Across Video Scenes for Temporal Video Grounding Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) aims to localize the temporal boundary of a specific segment in an untrimmed video based on a given language query.
